description: Curated plain-language symptom glossary v0 for user education and tooltips. Reviewed for safe medical wording (no diagnosis, no prescription recommendations).
disclaimer: This information is for informational and educational guidance only. It is not a medical diagnosis. Always consult a qualified healthcare professional.

entries.name: Fever
entries.plain_definition: A temporary increase in body temperature above normal (typically above 38°C or 100.4°F), often part of the body's natural defense against infection.
entries.when_to_seek_care: Seek urgent medical attention if temperature exceeds 39.4°C (103°F), lasts more than 3 days, or is accompanied by a stiff neck, confusion, or difficulty breathing.

entries.name: Chills or shivering
entries.plain_definition: Involuntary muscle shivering and feeling intensely cold, which commonly occurs as body temperature begins to rise during a fever.
entries.when_to_seek_care: Consult a doctor if chills are accompanied by uncontrollable shaking rigors, high fever, chest pain, or confusion.

entries.name: Tiredness or weakness
entries.plain_definition: An overwhelming feeling of tiredness, lack of energy, or physical weakness that does not improve with ordinary rest or sleep.
entries.when_to_seek_care: Seek medical advice if tiredness lasts more than two weeks, begins suddenly, or is accompanied by unintended weight loss or shortness of breath.

entries.name: Body or muscle aches
entries.plain_definition: Generalized, dull muscle soreness felt across multiple areas of the body, commonly experienced during viral infections or intense exertion.
entries.when_to_seek_care: Contact a doctor if muscle aches are severe, sudden, or accompanied by high fever, dark urine, or extreme muscle weakness.

entries.name: Sweating
entries.plain_definition: Producing more perspiration than usual, often as the body works to cool itself down during fever, physical activity, stress, or warm weather.
entries.when_to_seek_care: Seek immediate emergency medical attention if heavy sweating occurs suddenly with chest discomfort, dizziness, or shortness of breath.

entries.name: Night sweats
entries.plain_definition: Repeated episodes of extreme perspiration during sleep that soak nightclothes and sheets, even in a cool room.
entries.when_to_seek_care: Consult a healthcare professional if night sweats occur regularly or are accompanied by fever, chills, or unexplained weight loss.

entries.name: Unintended weight loss
entries.plain_definition: A noticeable decrease in body weight that occurs without changes in diet, appetite, or physical exercise routines.
entries.when_to_seek_care: Seek medical evaluation if you lose more than 5% of your body weight over 6 to 12 months without trying, or if accompanied by persistent fatigue.

entries.name: Loss of appetite
entries.plain_definition: A noticeable reduction in the desire to eat or feeling full very quickly after starting a meal.
entries.when_to_seek_care: Consult a doctor if poor appetite persists for more than a few days, or is accompanied by nausea, vomiting, or progressive weight loss.

entries.name: Dizziness or light-headedness
entries.plain_definition: Feeling lightheaded, unsteady, faint, or as if the room is spinning around you (vertigo).
entries.when_to_seek_care: Seek immediate medical attention if dizziness is accompanied by fainting, chest pain, slurred speech, or sudden numbness.

entries.name: Fainting
entries.plain_definition: A brief, temporary loss of consciousness and muscle posture, usually caused by a momentary drop in blood flow to the brain.
entries.when_to_seek_care: Seek immediate emergency medical attention (112) after any sudden fainting episode, especially if accompanied by chest pain, irregular heartbeat, or head injury.

entries.name: Swollen glands in the neck
entries.plain_definition: Enlarged or tender lymph nodes felt under the jaw or along the sides and back of the neck, commonly reacting to an infection.
entries.when_to_seek_care: See a doctor if neck glands are hard, fixed in place, continuously growing, or swollen for more than two weeks without signs of infection.

entries.name: Excessive thirst
entries.plain_definition: An unusually persistent, strong urge to drink liquids that is not satisfied by normal fluid intake.
entries.when_to_seek_care: Seek medical consultation if accompanied by frequent urination, unexplained weight loss, or persistent fatigue.

entries.name: Pale skin
entries.plain_definition: Skin that appears visibly lighter, duller, or washed out compared to normal complexion, often noticeable on the face, palms, or inside the lower eyelids.
entries.when_to_seek_care: Contact a doctor if paleness comes on suddenly, or is accompanied by dizziness, shortness of breath, rapid heart rate, or cold hands and feet.

entries.name: Passing little or no urine
entries.plain_definition: A substantial decrease in urination volume or frequency, passing little to no urine over several hours or throughout a full day.
entries.when_to_seek_care: Seek urgent medical care immediately if you have not passed urine in 8 to 12 hours, as this can indicate severe dehydration or kidney dysfunction.

entries.name: Unable to keep fluids down
entries.plain_definition: Repeatedly vomiting any fluids or liquids within minutes of drinking them, creating a risk of dehydration.
entries.when_to_seek_care: Seek prompt medical attention if you cannot keep liquids down for more than 12 to 24 hours, or if you notice dry mouth, dizziness, or dark urine.

entries.name: Wounds that heal slowly
entries.plain_definition: Minor cuts, scrapes, sores, or skin injuries that take an unusually long time to close, scab over, or heal completely.
entries.when_to_seek_care: Consult a healthcare provider if a wound shows signs of infection like worsening redness, swelling, warmth, pus discharge, or red streaks.

entries.name: Headache
entries.plain_definition: Pain, ache, or throbbing felt anywhere in the head, scalp, forehead, or temples.
entries.when_to_seek_care: Seek immediate emergency care (112) if the headache is sudden and explosively severe, or comes with a stiff neck, confusion, high fever, or vision changes.

entries.name: Sudden, very severe headache
entries.plain_definition: An excruciating headache that reaches peak intensity within seconds or minutes, often described as the worst headache of one's life.
entries.when_to_seek_care: Call emergency services (112) immediately. This requires urgent emergency department evaluation to rule out acute intracranial conditions.

entries.name: Sensitivity to light
entries.plain_definition: Discomfort, squinting, or pain in the eyes when exposed to normal or bright ambient light (photophobia).
entries.when_to_seek_care: Seek urgent medical care if light sensitivity appears suddenly with severe headache, stiff neck, high fever, or eye pain.

entries.name: Sensitivity to sound
entries.plain_definition: Discomfort, irritation, or pain triggered by normal every-day sounds or noises (phonophobia).
entries.when_to_seek_care: Consult a doctor if sound sensitivity is accompanied by severe headache, dizziness, or sudden hearing changes.

entries.name: Flashing lights or zig-zag lines in vision
entries.plain_definition: Temporary visual disturbances like shimmering zig-zag lines, blind spots, geometric patterns, or flashing lights, often preceding a migraine.
entries.when_to_seek_care: Seek medical advice if you experience visual aura for the first time, or if visual changes persist beyond one hour or occur with muscle weakness.

entries.name: Stiff neck
entries.plain_definition: Soreness and severe tightness in the neck that makes it painful or impossible to touch the chin to the chest.
entries.when_to_seek_care: Seek immediate emergency medical care (112) if neck stiffness occurs alongside high fever, severe headache, confusion, or light sensitivity.

entries.name: Tight neck or shoulder muscles
entries.plain_definition: Tightness, aching, or stiffness felt across the nape of the neck and the tops of the shoulders, commonly related to posture or stress.
entries.when_to_seek_care: Consult a healthcare provider if neck tension radiates down the arm, causes hand tingling or numbness, or follows an injury.

entries.name: Confusion or unusual drowsiness
entries.plain_definition: Difficulty thinking clearly, paying attention, remembering where you are, or unusual extreme drowsiness and disorientation.
entries.when_to_seek_care: Call emergency services (112) immediately. Sudden confusion or lethargy is a red-flag neurological emergency.

entries.name: Seizure (fit)
entries.plain_definition: An uncontrolled surge of electrical activity in the brain causing involuntary muscle jerking, body stiffening, blank staring, or loss of consciousness.
entries.when_to_seek_care: Call emergency services (112) immediately if a seizure lasts longer than 5 minutes, if multiple seizures occur, or if it is a person's first seizure.

entries.name: Face drooping on one side
entries.plain_definition: Weakness or sagging on one side of the face, often causing an uneven smile or inability to fully close one eye.
entries.when_to_seek_care: Call emergency services (112) immediately. Facial droop is a cardinal sign of stroke (FAST) requiring urgent emergency treatment.

entries.name: Weakness or numbness on one side of the body
entries.plain_definition: Sudden loss of strength, clumsiness, or numbness affecting one side of the face, arm, or leg.
entries.when_to_seek_care: Call emergency services (112) immediately. One-sided weakness is a cardinal stroke red flag requiring immediate emergency evaluation.

entries.name: Slurred or difficult speech
entries.plain_definition: Difficulty articulating words clearly, resulting in muffled, garbled, slow, or incomprehensible speech.
entries.when_to_seek_care: Call emergency services (112) immediately. Slurred speech is a major emergency sign of stroke or acute neurological compromise.

entries.name: Sudden loss of vision
entries.plain_definition: A rapid, unexpected loss of sight in one or both eyes, ranging from partial blurring or darkened patches to total blindness.
entries.when_to_seek_care: Call emergency services (112) immediately. Sudden vision loss requires immediate ophthalmological and neurological emergency evaluation.

entries.name: Numbness around the groin or buttocks
entries.plain_definition: Loss of sensation or numbness in the areas of the body that would touch a saddle, including the groin, buttocks, and inner thighs.
entries.when_to_seek_care: Seek emergency hospital care (112) immediately. Saddle numbness combined with back pain can indicate cauda equina syndrome, requiring urgent surgical evaluation.

entries.name: Loss of bladder or bowel control
entries.plain_definition: Inability to control urination or bowel movements, leading to unexpected incontinence or inability to empty the bladder.
entries.when_to_seek_care: Seek emergency medical attention (112) immediately, especially if accompanied by back pain, leg weakness, or saddle numbness.

entries.name: Runny nose
entries.plain_definition: Excess mucus draining from the nostrils, either watery and clear or thicker in consistency.
entries.when_to_seek_care: Consult a doctor if nasal discharge lasts more than 10 to 14 days, is accompanied by high fever, or drains from only one nostril with foul odor.

entries.name: Blocked or stuffy nose
entries.plain_definition: Swelling of the nasal passages and sinus linings causing a blocked, stuffy feeling that makes breathing through the nose difficult.
entries.when_to_seek_care: Seek medical advice if congestion lasts more than 10 days without improvement, or is accompanied by severe facial pain, forehead swelling, or high fever.

entries.name: Sneezing
entries.plain_definition: Involuntary, sudden expulsions of air from the nose and mouth triggered by irritation or inflammation of the nasal lining.
entries.when_to_seek_care: Consult a doctor if sneezing is severe, persistent, and accompanied by wheezing, facial pressure, or sinus pain.

entries.name: Sore throat
entries.plain_definition: A raw, painful, scratchy, or burning sensation in the throat that often worsens when talking or swallowing.
entries.when_to_seek_care: Seek medical evaluation if sore throat lasts more than a week, or urgent care if accompanied by difficulty swallowing saliva, breathing trouble, or high fever.

entries.name: Pain when swallowing
entries.plain_definition: Discomfort, sharp pain, or burning in the mouth or throat when swallowing food, liquids, or saliva.
entries.when_to_seek_care: Seek prompt medical evaluation if swallowing pain is severe, makes it impossible to swallow fluids, or is accompanied by drooling or neck swelling.

entries.name: Pain or pressure around the cheeks, eyes or forehead
entries.plain_definition: A feeling of fullness, aching, or heaviness centered around the cheeks, bridge of the nose, eyes, or forehead, often worsening when bending forward.
entries.when_to_seek_care: Contact a healthcare provider if facial pain is severe, accompanied by high fever, or associated with swelling or redness around the eyes.

entries.name: Thick yellow or green nasal discharge
entries.plain_definition: Sticky, thick mucus draining from the nose that is dark yellow or green in appearance.
entries.when_to_seek_care: See a doctor if thick nasal discharge persists for over 10 days, worsens after initially improving, or occurs with severe facial pain or fever.

entries.name: Loss of smell or taste
entries.plain_definition: A partial or complete inability to perceive scents (anosmia) or tastes (ageusia), often following viral respiratory infections.
entries.when_to_seek_care: Consult a doctor if sense of smell or taste does not begin to return after 2 to 4 weeks, or if it occurs alongside neurological symptoms like weakness or confusion.

entries.name: Swelling of the throat, lips or tongue
entries.plain_definition: Visible or felt enlargement of the tongue, lips, or back of the throat that can restrict the airway.
entries.when_to_seek_care: Call emergency services (112) immediately. Rapid swelling of the throat or tongue is a medical emergency that can indicate severe allergic reaction (anaphylaxis).

entries.name: Bleeding gums or nosebleeds
entries.plain_definition: Unexplained bleeding from the gums when brushing, or frequent spontaneous nosebleeds (epistaxis).
entries.when_to_seek_care: Seek prompt medical care if a nosebleed does not stop after 20 minutes of firm pressure, is heavy, or occurs alongside unusual bruising or fever.

entries.name: Cough
entries.plain_definition: A sudden, forceful reflex that clears the throat and breathing passages of irritants, mucus, or foreign particles.
entries.when_to_seek_care: See a doctor if a cough lasts longer than 3 weeks, produces blood, causes shortness of breath, or is accompanied by unexplained weight loss.

entries.name: Cough with mucus
entries.plain_definition: A 'wet' or 'chesty' cough that brings up phlegm or mucus from the lungs or bronchial airways.
entries.when_to_seek_care: Seek medical assessment if mucus is rust-colored, foul-smelling, or blood-streaked, or if accompanied by fever, chest pain, or breathing difficulty.

entries.name: Coughing up blood
entries.plain_definition: Coughing up blood or blood-streaked sputum from the respiratory tract (hemoptysis).
entries.when_to_seek_care: Seek urgent medical care (112) immediately. Coughing up more than small specks of blood requires urgent hospital evaluation.

entries.name: Shortness of breath
entries.plain_definition: Feeling breathless, winded, or like you cannot draw enough air into your lungs (dyspnea).
entries.when_to_seek_care: Call emergency services (112) immediately if breathlessness is sudden, severe, occurs while resting, or is accompanied by chest pain or blue lips.

entries.name: Wheezing
entries.plain_definition: A high-pitched whistling or squeaking sound heard when breathing, especially during exhalation, caused by narrowed airways.
entries.when_to_seek_care: Seek immediate emergency care (112) if wheezing is severe, sudden, or accompanied by struggling to breathe, chest tightness, or blue-tinted lips.

entries.name: Tight chest
entries.plain_definition: A feeling of constriction, heaviness, squeezing, or band-like pressure across the chest area.
entries.when_to_seek_care: Call emergency services (112) immediately. Chest tightness can signal a serious heart or lung emergency requiring immediate evaluation.

entries.name: Bluish lips or face
entries.plain_definition: A bluish or purplish discoloration of the lips, tongue, nail beds, or face (cyanosis), indicating low oxygen levels in the blood.
entries.when_to_seek_care: Call emergency services (112) immediately. Cyanosis is a critical medical emergency signaling acute oxygen deprivation.

entries.name: Red eye
entries.plain_definition: Bloodshot appearance of the white part of the eye (sclera) caused by dilated, irritated, or inflamed surface blood vessels.
entries.when_to_seek_care: Seek prompt medical attention if red eye is accompanied by eye pain, changes in vision, extreme light sensitivity, or clear pupil clouding.

entries.name: Itchy eyes
entries.plain_definition: An irritating, scratchy sensation on the surface or margins of the eyes that triggers an urge to rub them.
entries.when_to_seek_care: Consult an eye care professional if itching is severe, accompanied by thick discharge, swelling, or blurred vision.

entries.name: Watery eyes
entries.plain_definition: Excessive tearing or watering of the eyes caused by overproduction of tears or poor drainage through the tear ducts.
entries.when_to_seek_care: See an eye care professional if tearing lasts more than a few days, causes skin irritation, or occurs with eye pain or vision changes.

entries.name: Sticky discharge from the eye
entries.plain_definition: Sticky, crusty, yellowish, or greenish fluid that gathers in the corners of the eye or along eyelashes, often gluing eyelids shut in the morning.
entries.when_to_seek_care: Consult a doctor or ophthalmologist if discharge is heavy, greenish-yellow, or accompanied by eye redness, pain, or reduced vision.

entries.name: Pain behind the eyes
entries.plain_definition: An ache, pressure, or throbbing sensation felt deep behind the eyeballs or in the eye sockets, often worsening with eye movements.
entries.when_to_seek_care: Seek prompt medical evaluation if retro-orbital pain is severe, sudden, or accompanied by high fever, severe headache, or visual disturbances.

entries.name: Blurred vision
entries.plain_definition: A lack of sharpness or clarity in eyesight, making objects look hazy, fuzzy, or out of focus.
entries.when_to_seek_care: Seek immediate emergency care (112) if vision loss or blurring occurs suddenly, affects only one eye, or is accompanied by eye pain, headache, or weakness.

entries.name: Chest pain
entries.plain_definition: Discomfort, pressure, squeezing, heaviness, burning, or sharp pain felt in the center or left side of the chest.
entries.when_to_seek_care: Call emergency services (112) immediately. Any unexplained chest pain must be treated as a potential cardiac emergency until medically assessed.

entries.name: Pain spreading to the arm, jaw or back
entries.plain_definition: Discomfort originating in the chest that radiates outward to the left arm, both arms, shoulder, neck, jaw, or upper back.
entries.when_to_seek_care: Call emergency services (112) immediately. Radiating pain is a classic red-flag sign of acute myocardial infarction (heart attack).

entries.name: Fast or pounding heartbeat
entries.plain_definition: Sensations of a racing, pounding, fluttering, or skipping heartbeat that you feel in your chest, throat, or neck.
entries.when_to_seek_care: Seek emergency medical care (112) if palpitations occur with chest pain, shortness of breath, dizziness, or fainting.

entries.name: Nausea
entries.plain_definition: An uncomfortable, queasy feeling in the stomach with an urge or sensation that you might vomit.
entries.when_to_seek_care: Seek medical attention if nausea lasts more than 48 hours, prevents keeping fluids down, or is accompanied by severe abdominal pain.

entries.name: Vomiting
entries.plain_definition: The forceful expulsion of stomach contents upward through the mouth.
entries.when_to_seek_care: Seek immediate care if vomit contains blood or coffee-ground material, or if you cannot retain fluids for more than 24 hours.

entries.name: Diarrhoea
entries.plain_definition: Passing loose, watery, or liquid stools three or more times in a single day.
entries.when_to_seek_care: Consult a healthcare professional if diarrhea lasts more than 48 hours, causes dehydration, or contains blood or black stools.

entries.name: Constipation
entries.plain_definition: Infrequent bowel movements (fewer than three per week), difficulty passing stool, or hard, dry, painful stools.
entries.when_to_seek_care: Seek medical evaluation if constipation lasts over two weeks, comes on suddenly with severe abdominal pain, or is accompanied by vomiting.

entries.name: Abdominal (stomach) pain
entries.plain_definition: Aches, cramps, sharp twinges, or dull soreness felt anywhere between the bottom of the ribs and the groin.
entries.when_to_seek_care: Seek immediate emergency care (112) if stomach pain is sudden and severe, or accompanied by rigid belly, vomiting blood, or high fever.

entries.name: Pain in the lower right side of the abdomen
entries.plain_definition: Sharp, persistent, or worsening pain localized in the lower right quadrant of the belly, often intensifying with movement or coughing.
entries.when_to_seek_care: Seek emergency hospital care (112) immediately. Localized lower right abdominal pain is a classic indicator of appendicitis.

entries.name: Pain in the upper right side of the abdomen
entries.plain_definition: Aching or sharp pain located in the upper right quadrant of the abdomen beneath the ribs, often radiating toward the back or right shoulder.
entries.when_to_seek_care: Seek prompt medical attention if upper right abdominal pain is severe, lasts several hours, or is accompanied by fever, chills, nausea, or jaundice.

entries.name: Heartburn (burning behind the breastbone)
entries.plain_definition: A burning discomfort or pain felt behind the breastbone, often rising upward toward the neck or throat after eating or while lying down.
entries.when_to_seek_care: Consult a doctor if heartburn occurs more than twice a week, or seek emergency care (112) if chest burning feels like pressure or radiates to the arm or jaw.

entries.name: Sour taste or acid coming up into the mouth
entries.plain_definition: A sour, bitter-tasting fluid or undigested food backing up involuntarily from the stomach into the throat or mouth.
entries.when_to_seek_care: See a doctor if regurgitation occurs regularly, causes choking at night, or is accompanied by difficulty or pain when swallowing.

entries.name: Bloating
entries.plain_definition: A sensation of tightness, fullness, or visible swelling in the abdominal area, often associated with trapped gas.
entries.when_to_seek_care: Consult a doctor if abdominal bloating is persistent, worsens progressively, or occurs alongside unintentional weight loss or severe pain.

entries.name: Vomiting blood
entries.plain_definition: Throwing up bright red blood, dark clots, or material resembling dark coffee grounds (hematemesis).
entries.when_to_seek_care: Call emergency services (112) immediately. Vomiting blood indicates active upper gastrointestinal bleeding requiring emergency treatment.

entries.name: Black or bloody stool
entries.plain_definition: Passing bowel movements that appear pitch black and tarry (melena) or contain visible dark or bright red blood.
entries.when_to_seek_care: Seek emergency medical care (112) immediately. Black tarry or bloody stools indicate internal gastrointestinal bleeding.

entries.name: Yellow skin or eyes
entries.plain_definition: A yellowish tint affecting the whites of the eyes and the skin (jaundice), caused by elevated bilirubin levels.
entries.when_to_seek_care: Seek prompt medical evaluation. Jaundice signals potential liver, gallbladder, or blood disorders requiring timely clinical diagnosis.

entries.name: Dark urine
entries.plain_definition: Urine that appears unusually brown, dark amber, tea-colored, or cola-colored despite drinking normal amounts of water.
entries.when_to_seek_care: Consult a healthcare professional promptly, especially if dark urine is accompanied by yellowing eyes, pale stools, or abdominal pain.

entries.name: Pale stool
entries.plain_definition: Bowel movements that appear clay-colored, light gray, or chalky white, reflecting a lack of bile pigment.
entries.when_to_seek_care: Seek medical evaluation promptly. Pale stools indicate potential obstruction of the bile ducts or liver dysfunction.

entries.name: Burning or pain when passing urine
entries.plain_definition: A stinging, burning, or painful sensation felt during or immediately after passing urine (dysuria).
entries.when_to_seek_care: Consult a doctor promptly for urine testing, especially if accompanied by fever, back pain, or cloudy urine.

entries.name: Needing to pass urine often
entries.plain_definition: Needing to pass urine much more often than usual throughout the day or night, often with only small amounts passed.
entries.when_to_seek_care: See a doctor if increased frequency is new, persistent, or accompanied by burning, pelvic pain, or excessive thirst.

entries.name: Pain low in the abdomen
entries.plain_definition: Aching, pressure, or cramping located low in the pelvic or suprapubic area, just above the pubic bone.
entries.when_to_seek_care: Consult a doctor if pelvic pain is severe, worsens steadily, or is accompanied by painful urination, vaginal or penile discharge, or fever.

entries.name: Cloudy or strong-smelling urine
entries.plain_definition: Urine that looks milky, turbid, or hazy, or has an unusually strong, foul, or pungent odor.
entries.when_to_seek_care: Consult a healthcare professional if cloudy or smelly urine lasts more than 24 hours or occurs with burning urination or pelvic discomfort.

entries.name: Blood in urine
entries.plain_definition: Urine that appears pink, red, or brownish due to the presence of red blood cells (hematuria).
entries.when_to_seek_care: Seek prompt medical evaluation. Any visible blood in the urine requires clinical investigation by a healthcare professional.

entries.name: Pain in the side or back, below the ribs
entries.plain_definition: Sharp, aching, or throbbing pain felt in the side of the torso or mid-to-upper back, below the ribs and above the hips.
entries.when_to_seek_care: Seek prompt medical attention if flank pain is severe, radiates toward the groin, or is accompanied by fever, chills, nausea, or blood in the urine.

entries.name: Joint pain
entries.plain_definition: Aching, soreness, stiffness, or throbbing felt in one or more joints, such as the knees, hips, fingers, wrists, or ankles.
entries.when_to_seek_care: See a doctor if joint pain is accompanied by swelling, warmth, redness, or inability to bear weight on the joint.

entries.name: Joint swelling
entries.plain_definition: Visible puffiness, enlargement, or fluid accumulation around a joint, often making movement stiff and uncomfortable.
entries.when_to_seek_care: Seek medical attention if a joint swells suddenly, is hot and red to the touch, or is accompanied by fever.

entries.name: Lower back pain
entries.plain_definition: Aching, stiffness, or sharp pain felt in the lumbar region of the back, between the bottom of the ribcage and the buttocks.
entries.when_to_seek_care: Seek urgent medical care (112) if back pain comes with numbness in the groin/buttocks, loss of bowel/bladder control, or leg weakness.

entries.name: Muscle stiffness
entries.plain_definition: A sensation of tightness and reduced flexibility in muscles that makes movement difficult, especially after rest or upon waking.
entries.when_to_seek_care: Consult a doctor if stiffness is severe, does not loosen up after movement, or is accompanied by joint swelling or muscle tenderness.

entries.name: Skin rash
entries.plain_definition: A noticeable change in the texture, color, or appearance of the skin, resulting in red, bumpy, blotchy, or irritated patches.
entries.when_to_seek_care: Seek urgent medical care if a rash spreads rapidly, develops blisters, covers a large area of the body, or occurs with fever.

entries.name: Itchy skin
entries.plain_definition: An uncomfortable, irritating sensation on the skin that triggers a strong desire to scratch (pruritus).
entries.when_to_seek_care: See a doctor if itching is severe, disrupts sleep, lasts more than two weeks, or occurs all over without an obvious rash.

entries.name: Dry skin
entries.plain_definition: Skin that feels rough, tight, flaky, or dehydrated, often prone to fine scaling or superficial cracks.
entries.when_to_seek_care: Consult a healthcare provider if dry skin develops deep cracks that bleed, becomes red and painful, or does not improve with moisturizers.

entries.name: Scaly or flaky skin
entries.plain_definition: Patches of skin covered with dry, peeling, silvery, or flaky layers of dead surface skin cells.
entries.when_to_seek_care: Consult a doctor or dermatologist if scaly patches are persistent, itchy, painful, or spread to multiple body areas.

entries.name: Ring-shaped rash
entries.plain_definition: A circular, raised red rash with a clear or less inflamed center and scaly outer borders, characteristic of fungal skin infections.
entries.when_to_seek_care: Consult a doctor or pharmacist for evaluation if the ring expands, becomes warm and tender, or does not respond to over-the-counter antifungal creams.

entries.name: Raised, itchy welts (hives)
entries.plain_definition: Raised, intensely itchy, red or skin-colored welts or plaques (urticaria) that appear suddenly on the skin and may shift location.
entries.when_to_seek_care: Call emergency services (112) immediately if hives appear with throat swelling, lip or tongue swelling, dizziness, or difficulty breathing.

entries.name: Swollen skin
entries.plain_definition: Localized fluid buildup causing puffiness, enlargement, or tightness of the skin and underlying tissues (edema).
entries.when_to_seek_care: Seek emergency medical care if swelling is sudden, affects the face, lips, or throat, or is accompanied by breathing difficulty.

entries.name: Small itchy bumps
entries.plain_definition: Tiny, raised pimple-like bumps on the skin that cause intense itching, especially at night or in skin folds.
entries.when_to_seek_care: Consult a healthcare provider if itchy bumps spread across the body, affect household members, or develop honey-colored crusts.

entries.name: Thin lines or tracks on the skin
entries.plain_definition: Thin, raised, wavy, grayish-white or skin-colored lines on the skin surface, often seen between fingers or on wrists (scabies tracks).
entries.when_to_seek_care: See a doctor for confirmation and appropriate treatment for yourself and close household contacts.

entries.name: Pimples
entries.plain_definition: Small, inflamed, red, pus-filled bumps (papules or pustules) that form when hair follicles become clogged with oil and dead skin cells.
entries.when_to_seek_care: Consult a doctor or dermatologist if acne lesions are deep, painful, leave scars, or do not respond to over-the-counter care.

entries.name: Blackheads or whiteheads
entries.plain_definition: Small clogged pores that appear as dark, open plugs (blackheads) or tiny, closed flesh-colored bumps (whiteheads).
entries.when_to_seek_care: Consult a healthcare provider or dermatologist if comedones become extensively inflamed or turn into painful cysts.

entries.name: Oily skin
entries.plain_definition: Skin that appears shiny, greasy, and has visibly enlarged pores, caused by overactive sebaceous (oil) glands.
entries.when_to_seek_care: Consult a dermatologist if excess oil is accompanied by persistent cystic acne, redness, or flaking skin.

entries.name: Fluid-filled blisters
entries.plain_definition: Small bubbles or vesicles on the skin filled with clear watery fluid, blood, or pus, resulting from friction, burns, or infection.
entries.when_to_seek_care: Seek prompt medical attention if blisters cover large areas, appear on the face, eyes, or genitals, or show signs of spreading infection.

entries.name: Red skin that is spreading
entries.plain_definition: An area of red skin discoloration that visibly expands and spreads outward over hours or days, often warm and tender.
entries.when_to_seek_care: Seek urgent medical care promptly. Spreading redness can indicate an expanding bacterial skin infection (such as cellulitis) needing antibiotic evaluation.

entries.name: Warm, painful skin
entries.plain_definition: An area of skin that feels hot to the touch and causes soreness or pain when lightly pressed.
entries.when_to_seek_care: Seek medical evaluation promptly, especially if accompanied by spreading redness, swelling, pus drainage, or fever.

entries.name: Rash that does not fade when a glass is pressed on it
entries.plain_definition: A rash of small red or purple spots (petechiae or purpura) that does not fade or turn pale when a clear drinking glass is pressed firmly against it.
entries.when_to_seek_care: Call emergency services (112) immediately. A non-blanching rash can be a critical red flag for meningococcal disease or serious systemic bleeding.
lay_terms: spots that don't disappear with pressure

entries.name: Hot, dry skin
entries.plain_definition: Skin that feels hot to the touch and lacks normal perspiration, often occurring when the body's cooling mechanism fails during heat exposure.
entries.when_to_seek_care: Call emergency services (112) immediately. Hot, dry skin combined with high body temperature and confusion is a hallmark of heatstroke, a life-threatening emergency.

entries.name: Thoughts of self-harm or suicide
entries.plain_definition: Recurring thoughts, urges, or impulses to inflict physical harm on oneself, or thoughts related to suicide.
entries.when_to_seek_care: Call emergency services (112) or the national mental health/suicide crisis helpline immediately. Immediate professional crisis support is essential.
